h.strategy: After listing and negating default assumptions, keep only the negations that a general mechanism supports. Candidate mechanisms: parent quality (strong parents leave little room to improve and have more to lose), redundancy (duplicate or similar options dilute each other's contribution), and bottlenecks (an option matters little when it is not on the path to the output, however strong it is). Prefer predictions in which a usually helpful edit becomes neutral or harmful in a common context, or a usually harmful edit becomes harmless. Avoid conditions that only a few parents satisfy. Spread hypotheses across different edited fields and condition fields. Give at least four 'lower' predictions where the intuitive guess would be 'higher'.

hyps.why: Node 2 only reaches the output through edge 5 and its conv gains are blocked when that edge is none (bottleneck), though node 2 still feeds nothing else.
Node 1 receives no input when edge 0 is none, so a strong conv on edge 4 has nothing to transform.
Edge 2 carries signal from node 1, which is dead when edge 0 is none, so the conv is off the live path.
A second strong conv into the output node is redundant when the direct edge 3 already has conv 3x3, so marginal gain diminishes.
Replacing a missing direct output edge with conv 3x3 recovers much more than upgrading an existing op, since the parent is weakest there.
Cutting edge 0 costs less when edge 4 is already none, because it then only feeds node 2 via edge 2, which is a redundant route.
Removing edge 4 is nearly harmless when node 1 is already disconnected, since the edge carries no signal.
An extra conv 1x1 on another output edge adds little when the direct edge already has conv 3x3 (redundancy, strong parent).
Upgrading edge 0 from skip_connect gains less than upgrading from none or pooling, since skip is already a decent op.
Edge 2 feeds node 2, whose only exit is edge 5, so improving it is wasted when edge 5 is none.
